extraction.name: RoboBench
extraction.description: A comprehensive benchmark for evaluating multimodal large language models as embodied brains for robotic manipulation across instruction comprehension, perception reasoning, generalized planning, affordance prediction, and failure analysis.
extraction.creator: Yulin Luo, Chun-Kai Fan, Menghang Dong, Jiayu Shi, Mengdi Zhao, Bo-Wen Zhang, Cheng Chi, Jiaming Liu, Gaole Dai, Rongyu Zhang, Ruichuan An, Kun Wu, Zhengping Che, Shaoxuan Xie, Guocai Yao, Zhongxia Zhao, Pengwei Wang, Guang Liu, Zhongyuan Wang, Tiejun Huang, Shanghang Zhang
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The benchmark datasets were built from open-source and in-house robotic data, with MLLM- and human-provided annotations. The paper describes separate workflows for instruction, perception, planning, affordance, and reflection tasks, including preprocessing, annotation, and Q&A format generation.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator, Experiments, Others
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Open-source and in-house robotic data; large-scale real-world robotic datasets; robotic videos; real robot data with type and view metadata; curated static attributes; Gemini-segmented video steps; RoboMIND execution-level failure data; human-labeled bounding boxes; daily-life scenarios rewritten into implicit instructions.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Explicit instructions were rewritten into implicit demand-based requests using LLMs; robot videos were converted into natural-language task descriptions and step sequences; natural-language steps were mapped to predefined function sequences; function arguments were instantiated from extracted objects; planning annotations were refined by human annotators; planning tasks were represented as DAGs and evaluated with an MLLM world simulator.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: General and task-specific filtering were applied during construction, including image quality and task validity checks and excluding single-arm data from dual-arm tasks. After construction, 20 professionally trained annotators validated linguistic clarity, answerability, and correctness. Majority-vote filtering removed items all models solved correctly and sent items all models failed to manual review and correction.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotations included task summaries, step-wise instructions with timestamps, metadata such as objects/actions/scenes/embodiments, manual annotations of relative positions and keypoint changes, human-labeled bounding boxes, and expert labels for execution-level failures. Planning tasks also used manually annotated DAGs and critical object-state milestones.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Gemini-generated structured annotations were refined by human annotators. For planning evaluation, a human study sampled 438 long-horizon tasks and expert annotators assigned holistic scores from 0 to 20. The paper also reports majority-vote review and correction for difficult items.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: 20 professionally trained annotators; expert annotators with prior training.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: LLMs were used to rewrite explicit instructions into implicit ones; Gemini was used to generate structured planning annotations and segment video steps; VLMs/detection models were used in the dataset construction pipeline; an MLLM was used as a world simulator for planning evaluation.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Embodiment type, viewpoint, object attributes, scene context, and navigation/memory-related information are included; no explicit collection of human sensitive attributes is described.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark is intended to advance robust embodied intelligence and robotic manipulation by improving evaluation of reasoning, planning, affordance understanding, and failure diagnosis.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The paper notes that existing benchmarks often rely on simulators or human daily-activity data and that RoboBench aims to narrow the sim-to-real gap; it also discusses limitations in cross-embodiment, cross-view, and rare-object reasoning coverage.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Current models still show weak implicit instruction grounding, spatiotemporal perception, cross-scenario planning, affordance understanding, and failure diagnosis. The benchmark also notes that planning and failure analysis remain challenging and that some tasks rely on curated or synthesized annotations due to limited real-world failure data.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking and evaluation of multimodal large language models for embodied robotic manipulation, including instruction comprehension, perception reasoning, generalized planning, affordance prediction, failure analysis, and leaderboard-style comparison.
